author: reek
body: Drives the REAL LIR lowering (IR/Lir.codex, via the `lir-dump` pass) over real lowered IR. Each straight-line, `if`, and scalar `match` function below is lowered to the flat LIR, structurally verified, and dumped; the non-lowerable ones (a call, an act block, a constructor-pattern match) are declined. There is no reimplementation here: the shapes are ordinary Codex, the compiler lowers them to IRExpr, and `-Passes lir-dump` runs `lower-def-to-lir` + `lir-check-func` over each and prints one line per definition to the compile log. The pinned answers live in `lir-check.lir-expected`, read off the real lowering and hand-checked.

author: reek
body: The default battery compiles this file with the DEFAULT pipeline (the LIR pass does not run) and checks the runtime output against `lir-check.expected` -- that pins that the functions actually COMPUTE correctly, so the LIR dump is being read against working programs.

author: reek
body: Each lowerable function also gets a `LIVE <name>: bN in {..}` line beside its `LIR` line, pinning the backward liveness (Section: Liveness in `Lir.codex`): a parameter is live at the entry block, the result vreg is live at the exit block, and a value is live across exactly the blocks between its definition and its last use.

author: reek
body: A third `ALLOC <name>: v0->r0 v1->r0 ... [alloc-check: ok]` line pins the linear-scan register assignment (Section: Allocator) and the allocation verifier's verdict on it (Section: Allocation Verifier). The assignment now shows register reuse -- two vregs with disjoint live ranges share a register (e.g. sl-mix's v2 reuses v0's) -- and sl-wide, with five live parameters over four registers, shows spill slots (`sN`). The verifier runs over the real allocation and accepts it; corrupting the assignment makes it fire.

author: reek
body: **These five are pinned by their VALUES first, and by their dump lines as well since 2026-07-19.** They were answers-only for a reason worth keeping written down: `build/lir-dump-test.ps1` ran `-Passes lir-dump`, and `-Passes` REPLACES the pipeline rather than adding to it, so the recording ran with `fold-constants` and `inline-leaf-calls` switched off. All five dumped as `call math-mod` with an ordinary compare while every one of them emitted something else, and this prose concluded the inliner "runs later, in the INLINE phase". It does not. It runs in the pass pipeline the flag was silently emptying.

author: reek
body: The harness now names the default passes alongside `lir-dump`, so the pin records the program that actually ships: `if-even`, `if-odd` and `if-mod4` dump as a single `test`, and -- this is the part that was unreachable before -- `if-mod3` dumps as `rem` and `if-mod-one` keeps its `cmp v1 #1`, so both guards on the fusion are now visible in the pin rather than resting on the answers alone.

author: reek
body: The last two are the negative half and they are the point of the pair. The fusion is guarded on a power-of-two divisor and on a comparison against zero, and a guard that nothing tests is a guard that is not there. Both are chosen so a broken guard changes an answer rather than merely a shape: `if-mod3 6` is 1, and a mask-2 fusion escaping onto it would say 0.

author: reek
body: `if-even` is called with negative arguments on purpose. The mask and the remainder do not agree in general -- they differ in sign and value for a negative dividend, because the remainder follows the quotient's rounding and the mask does not -- and they agree on zero-ness alone, which is exactly and only what the fusion asks. -4 is even and -5 is odd, and the fused form has to say so.

author: reek
body: That returned 60 instead of 0: `rgb-to-hsl` called red yellow, and `color-test` had been failing on the selector for as long as the leaf register file has existed. Drop the division and it does not reproduce. Drop a parameter and it does not reproduce. This is the shape.

author: reek
body: Pinned by its ANSWERS. No benchmark can see this -- it is a wrong answer, not a slow one -- and no verifier can either: the entry moves are emitted before the blocks and are not LIR instructions, so `[alloc-check: ok]` below is a verdict on a function whose prologue the verifier never looked at.

author: reek
body: The function result is a use. `s` is both the result and the source of the one join move the then-arm makes, and the else-arm's division keeps the dead let alive through simplification. A coalescer that counts only instruction operands sees a single use, folds the add into the join vreg, and the result reads a vreg nothing defines -- RAX by default, so the else path answered the division: coal-result 5 -2 said -50 where it must say 6. The then path answers 6 either way, which is why the shape survives a spot check.
